about: Own-words reads from the daily research task (ADMIS, Rabobank, Czapp and the news feed). fund_score: -1 bearish to +1 bullish, a judgement on the fundamental news only.

cotton.fundamental: With Dec in its final days the front quote has rolled to Mar, now near 82.3, so the jump on screens is mostly the roll rather than new demand. Old-crop Mar/May is the market to watch: Texas Plains losses still back a tighter crop, while high-grade certificated stocks into Dec delivery remain a risk for longs, not a comfort.
events: Front cotton quote rolls to Mar near 82.3 (Yahoo Finance/ICE)
Cotton slips early Tuesday before recovering (Barchart/Nasdaq)
Texas Plains drought trims dryland yields (Farm Progress)

sugar.fundamental: Mar is edging up to about 17.70, holding above the 17.56 break as the real stays near 5.91 after the fiscal plan passed. Nothing new from Brazil's centre-south crush or mill mix this afternoon, so the rebound is still positioning rather than a supply change.
events: Raw sugar Mar ~17.70, holding above 17.56 (Yahoo Finance/ICE)
Real steady near 5.91/USD after fiscal plan clears Congress (Bloomberg/Yahoo Finance)

coffee.fundamental: Dec arabica has slid about 2.5% to near 268 as rising ICE certified stocks keep easing worries over Dec deliverability from Brazil. The Colombia export cut is a modest offset; until certs stop climbing, the stock build dominates.
events: ICE certified arabica stocks keep rising (Barchart)
USDA trims Colombia export forecast by 760k bags (Daily Coffee News)

cocoa.fundamental: Recent reports point to Ivory Coast port arrivals picking up after rain-related transport delays, and talk of ample global supply is weighing on prices; rising ICE certified stocks support that. Offsets are El Niño risk to the mid-crop and EUDR-related premiums in Europe; no new Ghana COCOBOD news since the 2030 bean-export-ban plan.
events: Cocoa eases as supply concerns fade and arrivals improve (Barchart/Nasdaq)
EUDR preparations lift European cocoa premiums (Bloomberg)
El Niño risk flagged for West African output (ADMIS)
